new.title: Climb to the Armenian Yılankale above the corn fields
new.desc: Yılankale (Snake Castle) is a late 12th to 13th century Armenian fortress on a rocky ridge above the Ceyhan plain. The gatehouse carries a relief that may show King Hetum with two lions, and the name comes from local tales of snakes in the crevices.
new.tip: Entry is free; a road reaches the foot of the hill, but the last stretch to the upper bailey is a steep rocky scramble, so wear sturdy shoes. Go in spring or autumn, as the plain is very hot in summer.

new.title: Find the Hittite king's rock relief at Sirkeli Höyük
new.desc: Beside the Ceyhan river, the Sirkeli mound has a rock relief of the Hittite king Muwatalli II (13th century BC), considered the oldest known Hittite rock relief. Excavations of a tower-gate fortress of about 1300 BC suggest a major Hittite centre, possibly Lawazantiya.
new.tip: The relief sits by the old Misis-Ceyhan road, just across the river from Yılankale, so the two combine into one short trip. Open-air and free, with little shade.

new.title: Walk the walls and victory arch of Anavarza
new.desc: Anazarbus was a major Roman and Byzantine city of Cilicia, with a roughly 1,500 m city wall, a three-arched Victory Arch at the head of a colonnaded street, a theatre, a stadium, aqueducts and rock tombs. A medieval Armenian castle crowns the rock above the plain, and excavations by Çukurova University have run since 2020.
new.tip: Bring water and a hat, as the site is huge and mostly shadeless; spring is best, when the plain is green. Allow at least two hours and a car, as it lies in Dilekkaya village south of Kozan.
new.q: Anavarza Antik Kenti, Dilekkaya, Kozan, Adana

new.title: Climb Sis Castle above Kozan, capital of Armenian Cilicia
new.desc: Kozan Castle, medieval Sis, was the capital of the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia after Toros I took it in 1113. The ruins of the walls, towers and a monastery cover a rock about 400 m high above the town.
new.tip: The hilltop gives views over Kozan and the Çukurova plain; go in the late afternoon for softer light and cooler air. Check the access path with locals, as parts of the ruins are fenced.

new.title: See Feke Castle, the Rubenid stronghold of Vahka
new.desc: Feke Castle, Armenian Vahka, was the seat of the Rubenid dynasty until Levon II was crowned in 1199. Eight towers and a watchtower survive on a steep outcrop about 1,270 m high above the town.
new.tip: Feke lies about 120 km north of Adana in the Taurus, so make it a day trip with a stop at Kozan. Ask in town for the footpath to the walls.

new.title: Spot Saimbeyli Castle, the medieval Badimon, above the town
new.desc: Saimbeyli, formerly Hadjin, was a mountain town of Armenian Cilicia; its castle, known as Badimon in the Middle Ages, may be the Berdus listed in King Levon I's 1198 coronation. The ruins overlook the town in the Taurus foothills.
new.tip: Combine it with the Obruk Waterfall 5 km away. Access is informal, so ask at the town hall or tea houses for the best approach.

new.title: See the Noah's Ark floor mosaic at Misis Mosaic Museum
new.desc: The museum, opened in 1959 on the west bank of the Ceyhan river, shows 4th-century floor mosaics found at ancient Mopsuestia, including a well-known Noah's Ark panel. It stands beside the Misis mound and the Roman bridge.
new.tip: It is small, so allow an hour, and pair it with the Misis Bridge and the old caravanserai ruins. Check opening days before driving out, as Monday closures are common in Turkish museums.
new.q: Misis Mozaik Müzesi, Misis, Yüreğir, Adana

new.title: Cross the nine-arched Roman Misis Bridge over the Ceyhan
new.desc: The Misis Bridge over the Ceyhan (ancient Pyramos) dates to the 4th century and was repaired under Justinian I in the 6th. Legend says the healer Lokman Hekim dropped the paper with his immortality remedy into the river here.
new.tip: Park near the mosaic museum and walk the bridge and the riverbank. Traffic still uses it, so keep to the edge.

new.title: Walk the old port walls of Ayas Castle in Yumurtalık
new.desc: Ayas (Aegeae, Laiazzo) was a busy Cilician port where Marco Polo passed in 1271 and 1296; Crusaders, Armenians, Mamluks and the Ramazanoğulları fought over it. Walls of the land castle still stand beside the harbour.
new.tip: Walk the waterfront and then continue to Süleyman's Tower and the island castle. Late afternoon is best for light and heat.

new.title: See Süleyman's Tower, the 1536 pirate watchtower
new.desc: Süleyman's Tower is a five-sided two-storey watchtower built in 1536 under Sultan Süleyman I to guard the port of Ayas against pirates. It stands on the coast just west of Yumurtalık.
new.tip: It is a quick stop, best at sunset over the gulf. Combine it with the Ayas walls and the harbour.

new.title: Read the Phoenician and Luwian gate reliefs at Karatepe
new.desc: Karatepe-Aslantaş is a Late Hittite hilltop fortress of the 8th century BC, with gates carved with lions, reliefs and bilingual Phoenician and Hieroglyphic Luwian inscriptions. Founded as an open-air museum in 1958 in a national park, it is on Turkey's UNESCO tentative list.
new.tip: Reported hours are 10:00 to 19:00, closed Monday, but check locally. It is about 23 km from Kadirli, and the national-park forest around it is good for a picnic.
new.q: Karatepe-Aslantaş Açık Hava Müzesi, Kadirli, Osmaniye

new.title: Walk the colonnaded street of Hierapolis-Kastabala
new.desc: Kastabala-Hierapolis was a Hellenistic and Roman city and cult centre of Artemis Perasia, with a theatre, a long colonnaded street and, above, the 13th-century Bodrum Castle. Excavations since 2009 have pushed its history back several centuries.
new.tip: Open daily, 09:00 to 17:00 in winter and 10:00 to 19:00 in summer by the posted schedule. Keep clear of the castle itself, which has been fenced since the 2023 earthquake.
new.q: Kastabala Hierapolis Antik Kenti, Kesmeburun, Osmaniye

new.title: Explore the basalt Toprakkale fortress beside the D400
new.desc: Toprakkale Castle sits on a basalt outcrop just south of the D400 highway; it was the Kınık Castle of Ottoman times and a key Cilician Armenian and Mamluk stronghold. Rooms and passages can be explored, and conservation work resumed after the 2023 earthquakes.
new.tip: Entry is free; the ruins are rough, so wear closed shoes and stay out of fenced areas. Drivers on the D400 pass right by, making it an easy stop.

new.title: See the church-turned-mosque of Ala Camii in Kadirli
new.desc: Ala Mosque in Kadirli is a Byzantine church and monastery, possibly of the 5th century, converted into a mosque in the late 15th century. It reopened for prayer after 96 years, and restoration revealed old mosaics and a crypt.
new.tip: Respect prayer times and dress modestly. The mosque is central in Kadirli, so it fits a stop on the way to Karatepe.

new.title: Browse the trade figures at the Osmaniye City Museum
new.desc: The municipal museum shows wax figures of vanished local trades such as spoon making, saddle making and carpet weaving, plus tools and natural dyes. A room covers the French occupation after the First World War and local resistance figures.
new.tip: Entry has been reported free, and it is indoors, so it suits rainy days. About 600 items are on show.
new.q: Osmaniye Kent Müzesi, Karaoğlan Caddesi, Osmaniye

new.title: Visit the ruins of ancient Comana at Şar near Tufanbeyli
new.desc: Şar is the site of Comana in Cappadocia, called Hieropolis in Roman times, with a church whose west facade is an early model of late antique Cappadocian architecture and the Alakapı gateway. It lies in the Taurus a few kilometres north of Tufanbeyli.
new.tip: Roads are slow in the high Taurus, so combine it with Saimbeyli. Ask locally for the path to Alakapı.
new.q: Şar Antik Kenti, Şarköy, Tufanbeyli, Adana

new.title: See the Ottoman hans of Karataş, the 1608 Tarihi Han
new.desc: Karataş keeps two Ottoman-era inns: the Tarihi Han of 1608 and the Menzil Han built in 1782. The port town came under Ottoman rule in 1517 and was a trading stop on the Pyramos delta.
new.tip: Wander the old centre by the harbour and combine it with a fish lunch. Hours of the hans vary, so ask in town.

new.title: Watch flamingos at Akyatan Lagoon
new.desc: Akyatan is a 147 sq km Ramsar lagoon on the Çukurova coast, with more than 10,000 greater flamingos wintering and breeding marbled duck; around 250 bird species have been recorded. Loggerhead turtles also nest on the sand bar.
new.tip: Winter and spring migrations are best; bring binoculars and a telephoto lens. Access is via Tuzla or Küçük Karataş village, and water levels drop in drought years.
new.q: Akyatan Lagünü, Küçük Karataş, Karataş, Adana

new.title: Birdwatch at the Kırmıtlı bird sanctuary on the Ceyhan
new.desc: Kırmıtlı, in the Kastabala valley on the Ceyhan, has ponds, reeds and trees that attract over a hundred bird species and several threatened dragonflies. It is a recognised Important Nature Area about 15 km from Osmaniye.
new.tip: Dawn and dusk are best, with owls and nightjars calling in the evening. Combine with Kastabala nearby.

new.title: Swim at the long free Karataş public beach
new.desc: Karataş Plajı is a long fine-sand public beach about 47 km from Adana, popular with Adana families and usually not crowded. There is no entry fee, and swimming is possible in all seasons.
new.tip: Fish restaurants line the waterfront. It is hot and busy on summer weekends, so aim for weekday mornings.

new.title: Cool off on Zorkun Plateau in the Amanos mountains
new.desc: Zorkun is a summer plateau in the Nur (Amanos) mountains, about 26 km up an asphalt road from Osmaniye, where visitors from Adana and Osmaniye escape 40-degree lowland heat. Zorkun tava, a lamb, tomato and pepper dish cooked over a wood fire, carries a geographical indication.
new.tip: Go on a weekday in summer to avoid crowds. Ask at plateau shops for Zorkun tava, usually cooked at weekends.

new.title: Walk Belemedik's German railway valley by the Çakıt
new.desc: Belemedik is the former workers' settlement of the Berlin-Baghdad railway, with German-era stone ruins, a cemetery and centuries-old plane trees along the Çakıt creek. The line crosses the Taurus with dozens of tunnels.
new.tip: It is about 10 km from Pozantı, reached by road through Anbaş, and is at its best in autumn colour. There is a restaurant opened in 2019 and wooden bungalows.

new.title: Picnic at the Obruk Waterfall near Saimbeyli
new.desc: Obruk Waterfall is a karst spring cascade in a nature park about 5 km from Saimbeyli, with picnic tables and parking, free to enter. Flow is strongest from April to June.
new.tip: Never swim here; there have been drownings. Go in spring when it flows, as it dries in drought summers.
new.q: Obruk Şelalesi Tabiat Parkı, Yeşilbağlar, Saimbeyli, Adana

new.title: Wander Kozan's historic bazaar and Roman bridge
new.desc: Kozan's old centre has a historic covered market, the Hoşkadem mosque, a Roman bridge and old mansions at the foot of Sis Castle. Officials describe the district as holding an Assyrian castle, Roman bridge and Mamluk mosque within a small area.
new.tip: Visit in April when the orange groves flower. Combine with the castle climb.

new.title: Eat ciğer at Bağrıyanık Ciğer Salonu in Kozan
new.desc: Bağrıyanık Ciğer Salonu is a Kozan liver-kebab house rated 4.9 by thousands of reviewers on Restaurantguru. Charcoal-grilled ciğer is the local fast lunch in Adana province.
new.tip: Order ciğer with raw onion, sumac and ayran. Liver houses sell out, so go at lunch.
new.q: Bağrıyanık Ciğer Salonu, Ciğerciler Sokağı, Kozan, Adana

new.title: Eat kebap at Kebapçı Şevket in Ceyhan
new.desc: Kebapçı Şevket is a long-reviewed kebab house in Ceyhan with some 700 reviews on Restaurantguru. It is a plain local lokanta focused on charcoal-grilled meat.
new.tip: Go at lunch; ask for hot peppers and şalgam.
new.q: Kebapçı Şevket, Hükümet Caddesi, Ceyhan, Adana

new.title: Dine on fish at Balıkçı Fevzi Rıhtım in Karataş
new.desc: Balıkçı Fevzi Rıhtım Restoran ve Pansiyon sits on the quay at Karataş with a seafood menu and a guesthouse upstairs.
new.tip: Book a quayside table at sunset; fish is sold by weight.
new.q: Balıkçı Fevzi Rıhtım Restoran ve Pansiyon, Orman Caddesi, Yeni Mahallesi, Karataş, Adana

new.title: Eat ciğer at Ciğerci Enver Usta in Osmaniye
new.desc: Ciğerci Enver Usta Kebap Salonu is the highest-reviewed kebab house in Osmaniye on Restaurantguru, with over 1,000 votes at 4.8. Liver kebab is a standard breakfast and lunch there.
new.tip: Go for a late breakfast of ciğer with onions and bread.
new.q: Ciğerci Enver Usta Kebap Salonu, Dr. Devlet Bahçeli Bulvarı, Osmaniye

new.title: Eat Adana kebap at Biber Kebap on Hasan Çenet Caddesi
new.desc: Biber Kebap on Hasan Çenet Caddesi in the Esenevler neighbourhood is one of Osmaniye's top-rated kebab restaurants, at 4.8 from about 580 reviews.
new.tip: Try the kebap with grilled peppers; evenings are busiest.

new.title: Try biftek tantuni at Celal Usta in Osmaniye
new.desc: Celal Usta Biftek Tantuni is a tantuni shop in Osmaniye rated 4.9 from over 660 reviews on Restaurantguru. Tantuni is shredded beef cooked on a flat griddle and wrapped in lavaş.
new.tip: Order tantuni with onion and sumac; it is a cheap, quick stop.
new.q: Celal Usta Biftek Tantuni, Ahmet Demir Sokak, Osmaniye
